summary: This is a revised version of the Thermostat's display method: instead of printing the status to the console, it builds a message and hands it back to the caller as a String. Returning a value makes the method easy to test, because a test can compare the returned text against what it expects.

lines.text: The same Thermostat class from earlier in the chapter, shown here with only the one method that is changing.
A placeholder standing in for the fields, constructor, and getStatus method you already wrote; they stay exactly as they were.
The return type is now String rather than void, so the method produces a value that a test or another part of the program can inspect.
The label and the result of getStatus() are joined into one string and returned, replacing the earlier call to System.out.println so that nothing is written to the console.
